title: categorize airtable expense via uploaded audio
breadth_reason: This script tests Anticipy's ability to process a user's uploaded audio recording against a real signed-in Airtable surface, covering the full public product path from audio upload to surface proof.

v7_target.surface_rule: user's signed-in Chrome with Airtable tab open
v7_target.proof_rule: fresh surface-readable proof from the public build

primary_user_input.reason: Uploaded audio tests the ASR pipeline on a real mp3 file, ensuring coverage of the audio upload path rather than relying on pasted transcripts or live microphone capture.

real_user_surfaces.name: Airtable
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: visible Airtable record or signed-in workspace

real_user_surfaces.name: Audio Upload
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: audio/mpeg file with spoken reference text

moments.spoken_reference_text: Please update the Airtable Expenses record for the Brookline coffee charge from yesterday and tag it work meetings. If you cannot prove the visible Airtable record or my signed-in workspace, decline without changing anything.
moments.delivery_instruction: Use the Anticipy say command to produce a per-run audio artifact of the spoken reference text, then upload the resulting mp3 file via the /api/listen/upload endpoint.

success_criteria: The engine correctly transcribes the uploaded audio and extracts the intent to update an Airtable expense record.
The engine verifies the user's signed-in Airtable surface in Chrome before taking any action.
If the Airtable surface is visible and the record is found, the engine updates the record and tags it as 'work meetings'.
If the surface is not verifiable, the engine declines with a clear explanation and makes no changes.
All proofs are generated from the public build using fresh surface captures.
failure_triggers: The engine attempts to act without first verifying the signed-in Airtable surface.
The engine uses a transcript paste or live microphone instead of the uploaded audio file.
The engine modifies the Airtable record when the surface is not provably visible.
The engine uses stale screenshots, logs, or fixture data as proof.
The engine fails to produce a proof artifact tied to the public build.
